parameters.name: metric_column
parameters.description: numeric price_demand column to average, e.g. total_demand_mw or rrp

parameters.name: start_date
parameters.description: date at whose 00:00 the window starts, ISO YYYY-MM-DD, that 00:00 interval excluded

parameters.name: end_date
parameters.description: date at whose 00:00 the window ends, ISO YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive of that 00:00 interval

sql_template: SELECT region, round(avg({metric_column}), 1) AS value FROM price_demand WHERE settlement_ts > CAST('{start_date}' AS TIMESTAMP) AND settlement_ts <= CAST('{end_date}' AS TIMESTAMP) GROUP BY region ORDER BY region

steps.cmd: fill every slot of sql_template from the question's declared parameters and save it as filled.sql
steps.pass: filled.sql contains no remaining {slot} and names only columns of price_demand
the JSON prints columns [region, value] with one row per region and carries no error key
PASS question, PASS sql, PASS values

notes: settlement_ts is the END of the 5-minute interval, so a day's 288 intervals carry timestamps from 00:05 of that day up to and including 00:00 of the next day; filter with > start and <= end, because a >= start AND < end window drops the last interval.
average the raw column and round once at the end - rounding each interval first changes the reported figure.
the region comes from the row itself, so no unit-to-region join is needed for this shape.
